title: Aerogel Blanket Applications: Oil & Gas, EV Batteries, Construction, and Industrial Insulation
content:
Aerogel blanket is one of the most commercially important aerogel product formats on the market today. Search demand around aerogel blanket applications continues to rise because project teams want materials that combine thermal performance with installability. A blanket format is easier to wrap, cut, fit, and integrate into real industrial systems than many rigid alternatives.

In this article, we look at the main application sectors where aerogel blanket products are most relevant and why buyers increasingly compare aerogel options when evaluating insulation upgrades.

What is an aerogel blanket?

An aerogel blanket is typically a flexible insulation composite made by integrating aerogel into a fibrous reinforcement matrix. The structure helps deliver low thermal conductivity while maintaining enough flexibility for practical handling and installation. This is especially useful for curved surfaces, removable insulation covers, and retrofit environments where geometry is irregular.

1. Oil and gas insulation

Oil and gas remains one of the best-known application areas for aerogel blanket insulation. Facilities often contain dense process layouts, long pipe runs, valves, vessels, and equipment requiring thermal control. When insulation thickness affects access, weight, or heat retention, aerogel blanket can become attractive.

Common use cases include:

  • Hot process piping
  • Offshore modules where weight matters
  • Subsea or exposed environments depending on system design
  • LNG and cryogenic service in selected insulation architectures

2. Refining and petrochemical plants

Refineries and petrochemical sites often need insulation solutions that balance thermal performance, maintenance access, and long service life. Aerogel blanket may support thinner insulation builds in congested areas while helping reduce heat loss in process systems. Decision-makers usually compare it against mineral wool, calcium silicate, or other established products based on operating temperature, corrosion-under-insulation strategy, and installed system requirements.

3. Industrial insulation and removable covers

Aerogel blanket is frequently discussed for removable insulation pads, turbines, exhaust lines, steam systems, and compact industrial equipment. The blanket format is valuable because it can conform around flanges, valves, and custom housings. For maintenance teams, easier access and reinstallation can matter almost as much as thermal performance.

4. Building envelope and retrofit projects

In construction, aerogel blanket or aerogel-enhanced insulation systems are often evaluated for situations where space is limited. Historic building retrofits, high-value facades, thin wall assemblies, and specialty glazing-adjacent systems are common examples. In these cases, every millimeter matters. A thinner insulation layer can preserve interior space or simplify detailing where bulkier conventional materials create design conflicts.

5. EV battery and thermal management systems

Battery safety and thermal propagation control have pushed more attention toward advanced thermal materials. Aerogel-based barriers and composite formats are now frequently mentioned in EV battery pack discussions. While not every solution is literally a blanket product in the industrial-insulation sense, aerogel-derived flexible thermal barriers are relevant because they combine low conductivity with lightweight integration potential.

For engineers, the important point is not hype but fit-for-purpose design. The right product depends on pack architecture, mechanical requirements, fire-test criteria, manufacturability, and cost targets.

6. Aerospace, rail, marine, and specialty transportation

Transportation sectors care deeply about weight, space, and safety. That makes aerogel blanket and aerogel composite materials interesting for specialty transportation applications ranging from rail systems to marine equipment and aerospace thermal protection concepts. Qualification requirements are strict, but the design logic is consistent: high thermal performance in constrained envelopes.

What makes aerogel blanket attractive across sectors?

  • Thin insulation profiles for tight spaces
  • Reduced weight compared with some traditional systems
  • Flexibility for complex shapes and curved surfaces
  • Potential installation advantages in retrofit work
  • Strong interest in energy efficiency and thermal safety applications

Selection factors before specifying aerogel blanket

Not all aerogel blankets are identical. Before shortlisting a product or supplier, evaluate:

  • Target temperature range
  • Mechanical robustness and compressibility
  • Hydrophobic performance and environmental durability
  • Thickness options and installation method
  • Relevant certifications and application case history
  • Regional supply, lead time, and technical support

FAQ: aerogel blanket applications

What industries use aerogel blanket most often?

Industrial insulation, oil and gas, refining, construction retrofit, and advanced thermal management are among the most common discussion areas.

Why is aerogel blanket popular in retrofit projects?

Because it can offer strong insulation performance in thinner sections, which is valuable when existing structures leave little room for additional thickness.

Is aerogel blanket only for high-temperature systems?

No. Product suitability depends on the specific formulation and system design. Some applications focus on hot service, while others involve cryogenic or battery-related thermal control.

Conclusion

Aerogel blanket applications continue to expand because the format fits real-world installation needs. It is not simply a laboratory material; it is a practical insulation option for sectors where geometry, thickness, energy efficiency, and safety all matter. As more industries prioritize compact high-performance thermal systems, aerogel blanket will remain a high-intent search topic for engineers, buyers, and technical decision-makers.
